A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLaDA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original model training, scaling experiments, benchmark evaluations, sampling ablations, iGSM results, and poem-completion experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and reports additional sampling, classifier-free guidance, throughput, and memory analyses.

M1.justification: The architecture, masking objective, pre-training, and SFT procedures remain unchanged. V3 introduces an inference adjustment that sets EOS-token confidence to zero during pure-diffusion Instruct sampling on five benchmarks (Appendices B.4 and B.6). The renamed fixed-length 'block diffusion LLaDA' strategy corresponds to v1's semi-autoregressive remasking.

E1.justification: The training corpora and benchmark/task coverage are retained, including the standard language benchmarks, iGSM, and 496 Chinese poem pairs. Added guidance, sampling, and efficiency experiments reuse existing tasks. V3's additional corpus-composition information documents existing training data rather than establishing a coverage change.

E2.justification: The main benchmark and poem-completion comparator rosters remain unchanged. However, v3 adds autoregressive and variable-length block-diffusion samplers to the sampling comparisons, alongside the retained fixed-length strategy. Its efficiency analysis also compares against LLaMA3 with and without KV caching, whereas v1's sampling-step analysis evaluated only LLaDA. These additions substantially expand the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: V1 uses tuned classifier-free guidance on six likelihood benchmarks and block sampling for several Instruct benchmarks; v3's main results omit guidance and use pure diffusion. Instruct generation lengths also change, including GSM8K from 256 to 512 and GPQA from 128 to 64. Base-model generation evaluation switches to lm-evaluation-harness except HumanEval-FIM. Ablation settings are revised, and throughput and memory protocols are added.

E4.justification: V3 replaces the GSM8K-only remasking comparison with broader sampling-strategy and remasking analyses, adds a six-benchmark guidance ablation, and expands sampling-step analysis into speed-quality and memory studies. The length ablation expands to five Base-model tasks but drops the Instruct-model sweep. The iGSM analysis and dialogue case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that the 8B pre-training and SFT experiments were executed once and retain the same one-sample or 128-sample Monte Carlo likelihood-estimation practice. V3 adds no seed reporting, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Many benchmark values and rankings change. In Table 2, LLaDA Instruct GSM8K changes from 78.6 to 69.4, Math from 26.6 to 31.9, and MBPP from 34.2 to 41.0. Its poem forward/reversal scores change from 48.8/42.4 to 51.8/45.6. Given revised evaluation and decoding settings, these are revised results rather than established same-setting gains or losses. V3 also adds substantial ablation and efficiency results; iGSM scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, likelihood bound, equivalent masking objectives, any-order autoregressive connection, and guidance formula are retained in Equations (1)-(16). V3 adds explanatory comparisons and expands attribution, but introduces no substantive new theorem, proof, assumption, or derivation.

C1.justification: V3's abstract moderates 'outperforming' the self-constructed ARM baselines to performing comparably. The introduction also frames its question around specific core capabilities rather than LLM intelligence broadly. The principal contributions concerning scaling, in-context learning, instruction-following, and reversal reasoning remain intact.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations linking multidirectional conditioning to generalization, autoregressive Instruct failures to complete-sentence SFT data, and KV-cache speedups to prompt length (Section 3.1 and Appendices B.4/B.7). It also interprets low-confidence remasking through reduced diversity, identifies fixed generation length as an efficiency limitation, and explicitly limits claims of general speed superiority.

D1.justification: V3 newly documents corpus sources, the 11% Chinese/61% English/28% code mixture, cleaning and BERT-based quality filtering, and the SFT split of one million human and 3.5 million synthetic samples. It adds baseline learning rates, batch sizes and tuning information, detailed scaling checkpoints, and A100-80GB/bfloat16/batch-size-one efficiency settings. These are substantial documentation additions, without evidence of changed training corpora or retraining.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning through discussion of concurrent Mercury, protein diffusion, and sampling-acceleration and distillation research. It explicitly contrasts its objective with MaskGIT and broadens foundational attribution to Shi and Sahoo alongside Ou. Magpie and Magicoder are added for synthetic-data methodology. These changes go beyond citation-style and bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the method, theory, and case-study prose are retained. V3 edits the framing and explanations, renames semi-autoregressive remasking, reorganizes Appendix B, and moves the Impact Statement to Appendix C. These refine the existing narrative rather than replace its overall structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 gains an Instruct panel, Figure 4 becomes a three-strategy diagram, and Figure 5 replaces sampling-step plots with four throughput-quality plots. Ablation and memory tables are added or substantially restructured. Tables 18-19 newly tabulate the existing scaling figure, while several case-study displays are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially improves the interpretability and reproducibility of the empirical claims. It separates unguided pure-diffusion main results from guidance and block-decoding alternatives, tests sampling choices across multiple tasks, measures speed and memory, and supplies important data-preparation and baseline-training details. This addresses v1's limited characterization of dependence on inference choices and practical resource costs. These gains outweigh the removal of the Instruct length sweep, although statistical uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.
